verify.note:
── PROBE TIGHTENED 2026-08-24 (HYG-016). It used to assert 'exactly one rmSync in the file', a PROXY for the invariant that actually matters: deletes INTO .next/cache are restricted to the named compiler list and can never reach the fetch cache. When check:cache-budget gained a second, unrelated delete — orphaned pnpm store entries under node_modules/.pnpm — the proxy fired and the invariant was untouched. It now classifies every rmSync by its TARGET: exactly one may name cacheDir/.next/cache and it must sit inside the COMPILER_CACHE_DIRS loop, and every other delete must name node_modules/.pnpm. That is strictly stronger than the count it replaced — the new delete path is pinned too, so an edit that repoints it at the cache fails this row rather than passing it.

── PROBE RE-POINTED 2026-09-30 (HYG-140, ADR-1656). The hold added a second, guarded delete into .next/cache, and the one-delete count fired on it the way the one-rmSync count fired on HYG-016: a proxy, with the invariant untouched. It now allows exactly TWO deletes into the cache. One must sit in the top-level loop over COMPILER_CACHE_DIRS, as before. The other must sit in a named function whose body checks HOLD_ARTIFACTS.includes and throws before its rmSync. HOLD_ARTIFACTS must resolve to plain string constants naming neither fetch-cache, images, anything in NEVER_TRIM_DIRS nor a compiler cache. Every renameSync must sit in holdSwap. Every other arm is unchanged. Mutation-fired: fetch-cache or images added to HOLD_ARTIFACTS, a bare rmSync into cacheDir, the trim loop moved off COMPILER_CACHE_DIRS, the HOLD_ARTIFACTS guard removed, a renameSync outside holdSwap.

append.detail: PROBE RE-POINTED 2026-09-30 (HYG-140, ADR-1656). check:cache-budget gained a hold: it can put back the compiler cache a build restored instead of trimming it. That adds deletes of the hold's own scratch (the snapshot, the set-aside cache, the count file), all routed through one helper, dropHoldArtifact(), which refuses any name outside HOLD_ARTIFACTS. The probe now allows that one guarded site beside the trim loop and pins what HOLD_ARTIFACTS may name, so the guarantee is unchanged: only the named compiler caches can be deleted by the trim, and fetch-cache and images can never be deleted. Status stays done.
